text: Generative Project: From Words to Worlds - Text-to-Image Generation Using Transformer and Diffusion Models Course: IE 7615 Deep Learning for AI Focus Area: Generative Deep Learning Models 1. Overview Generative modeling has revolutionized how AI systems create visual content from textual descriptions. This project challenges you to design and implement a text-to-image generation pipeline by integrating Transformer-based text encoders and Diffusion- based image generators. Through this project, you will gain hands-on experience with conditional generative models, latent representations, and cross-modal learning-the key foundations of modern AI systems such as DALL-E, Midjourney, and Stable Diffusion.

2. Objectives By the end of this project, students will: Understand the architectural principles behind Transformers and Diffusion Models. Implement or fine-tune a conditional diffusion model using text embeddings as conditioning input. Explore how text-image alignment and multimodal representations work. Evaluate generated results quantitatively and qualitatively. Reflect on ethical and societal implications of generative AI. 3. Project Description Core Tasks 1. Dataset Preparation

Use a paired image-caption dataset (e.g., COCO Captions, Flickr30k, or a smaller curated set*). Preprocess text using a Transformer-based embedding model (e.g., CLIP, BERT). Normalize and resize images for consistent input dimensions. 2. Model Implementation Use a pre-trained Diffusion Model (e.g., Stable Diffusion or DDPM) and condition it on text embeddings. Experiment with: Varying noise schedules and sampling steps. Different conditioning strengths. Guidance scaling (classifier-free or text-guided diffusion). 3. Evaluation Quantitatively assess image quality using FID (Fréchet Inception Distance) or IS (Inception Score).

Qualitatively evaluate semantic alignment between generated images and text prompts. Visualize and present generated examples. 4. Analysis and Reflection Discuss challenges in text-image conditioning. Highlight trade-offs between fidelity and diversity. Reflect on potential ethical concerns (e.g., dataset bias, content generation misuse). 4. Deliverables 1. Project Report (6-8 pages) Introduction, background, and related work Methodology and model architecture

Experimental setup and results Analysis and discussion Ethical considerations and conclusion 2. Generated Results Gallery Showcase examples of text prompts and corresponding generated images. 3. Source Code Repository Well-documented code with clear dependencies and instructions. 4. Presentation (~10-15 minutes) Summarize goals, approach, and key findings. 5. Suggested Tools & Frameworks Programming: Python, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers Pre-trained Models: CLIP, Stable Diffusion, DDPM, Denoising Diffusion Implicit Model (DDIM) Datasets: COCO Captions, Flickr30k, or a small subset of LAION-400M 6. Evaluation Criteria Category Description Weight Technical Correctness, efficiency, and originality of model 30% Implementation integration Experimental Results Quality and diversity of generated images 25% Analysis & Discussion Depth of analysis and reflection on findings 20%
Report Quality Clarity, organization, and presentation 15% Reproducibility Code organization and documentation 10% 7. Suggested Milestones
